dedupe_keys.name: the global value of mangroves for risk reduction

description: The Global Value of Mangroves for Risk Reduction quantifies the coastal flood protection that mangroves give to people and property worldwide and ranks countries by these benefits relative to their vulnerability. The Nature Conservancy and the Environmental Hydraulics Institute IH Cantabria produced it with hydrodynamic and economic models, valuing mangroves as avoided flood damages in the way engineering and insurance practice values defences. Coverage is the world's mangrove coasts; results are mapped as the difference in annual expected damages with and without mangroves per 100 km of coast. Findings include that mangroves reduce annual flooding for more than 18 million people and that damages would rise by over US$82 billion a year without them. Format and access: a summary report, a technical report and map layers on the Coastal Resilience site. Licence: Coastal Resilience terms of use, not read in detail; free to view. Caveats: results are model estimates at coarse coastal segments, the reference year is not stated on the page, and property values drive the rankings. It supports hazard exposure, climate adaptation and investment cases for mangroves as natural coastal infrastructure. Related catalogue records are the InVEST coastal vulnerability model and the World Bank NbS Opportunity Scan.
